subject: Making a figure to be squared shaped

messages.author: fca01f44f8b824c4
messages.subject: Making a figure to be squared shaped
parts:
Hello,

I have produced a figure in ggplot2 and by default the figure comes framed into rectangles. A professor requested me to change those rectangles to squares because  rectangles have been described as "misguiding the eye" and hiding disproportional changes. I do not think that changing the x scale will help. I found some information about modifying the graph with grid, but I am unsure about which direction is the best for this. Any advise would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

Paola


Here is the code I used and the figure produced:

Ecprc<-ggplot(data=Exprc, aes(x=plant_extinction, y=ant_extinction, group=group, colour=group))+geom_line()+geom_point()

Ecprc<-Ecprc+scale_colour_grey()+theme_bw()

Ecprc<-Ecprc+labs(x="Plant extinction", y="Ant extinction")

Ecprc<-Ecprc+facet_wrap(~country, ncol=1)

Ecprc

messages.subject: Re: Making a figure to be squared shaped
parts:
You are possibly looking for coord_equal():
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/coord_equal.html

The easiest ways to adjust the overall size and aspect ratio of the
plot are with the width and height arguments to your graphics device,
or by plotting to a graphics window, adjusting it to be the size you
want, and then using ggsave().
